Subject: Eval handshake + acceptance timetable — GPU rightsizing & MAP close

Carlos / Samantha —

Great demo last week, thanks for the time. Attaching a clean MAP draft and our current lead-time estimate for H100 reservations. I'd like to align on a tight eval -> reserve path so you can get predictable throughput for your clinical ingestion workload. High-level ask: confirm whether NovaMed can commit to a two-tranche reservation (pilot + full capacity) and the target activation week.

Proposed MAP highlights (short):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize MAP doc and procurement owner (you)
- Week 1-2: eval sprint (baseline prompts, perf targets, 2k concurrent tokens/day)
- Week 3: acceptance window (SLO sign-off, latency P50/P95 checks, sample pass rate)
- Week 4-8: provisioning and onboarding to Dedicated GPU pool (tranche 1 live)
- Week 9-12: tranche 2 activation to hit target pool size

Questions for you now:
1) Do you need single-region (us-west) or multi-region?
2) Can procurement sign a PO within 3 weeks of acceptance?
3) Any hard constraints on lead time (e.g., must be live by Dec 15)?

Attachments: MAP_NovaMed_v0.3.xlsx (spreadsheet) | H100_leadtime_estimate.pdf (pdf)

Proposed next step: 30-min handshake call this Thursday to lock the timelines. Marissa and Karthik are copied for technical + commercial gating.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

- Procurement wants the minimum guaranteed throughput (tokens/sec) you recommend for the pilot vs full tranche. They'll use that to size internal test harness.
- We prefer a two-tranche approach (pilot -> full) but need clarity on whether tranches can be staggered by region.
- Can you provide SOC 2 evidence and a short runbook our security team can review? Procurement will not sign without those items.

We can do Thursday morning PT. Looping in procurement email so they see the attachments.

Subject: Re: Eval handshake + acceptance timetable — GPU rightsizing & MAP close

Samantha / Carlos —

Quick technical notes to help procurement and security:

1) Throughput guidance (baseline):
- Pilot tranche (small): 8 H100-80GB equivalent tokens/sec peak (target for eval prompts)
- Full tranche: scale to 32 H100-80GB equivalent tokens/sec (target for production ingest)

2) Lead times & tranches: 
- Dedicated H100 pool (new reservation): typical procurement -> provisioning is ~10-12 weeks in our baseline supply scenario.
- If you need faster ramp, we can propose a hybrid start: begin with a smaller Dedicated A100 tranche (~3-4 weeks) for the eval, then migrate to H100 tranche when available. That reduces risk for the Dec timeline.

3) Acceptance checklist (what we test during acceptance window):
- Latency: P50 < 100ms, P95 < 350ms for typical sample set
- Correctness: sample pass rate >= 92% on the agreed eval prompt set
- Stability: no more than 1% error rate over 24h soak

4) Security artifacts: SOC2 type II summary and encrypted audit log sample available; sharing link in chat during call.

I've attached a short lead-time breakdown (H100_leadtime_estimate.pdf). We'll bring an engineer to the call to step through any technical gating items.

- Marissa
Technical Account Lead, Onboarding | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Eval handshake + acceptance timetable — GPU rightsizing & MAP close

Carlos / Samantha —

Following up from our call — appreciate the openness on tranches. From a commercial perspective:

- Proposed commercial flow: 6-month reserved commitment (tranche 1: 25% capacity for pilot at reduced rate, tranche 2: remaining 75% on 30-day notice)
- If Novamed signs within 3 weeks of acceptance, we can offer a 7% commit discount and a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration engineering (applied to month 1).
- Need to capture the deal in HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/7312 — please confirm the procurement PO number and a billing contact.

Ben (cc) will coordinate SOW language for the acceptance criteria and will produce a short mutual action checklist we can attach to the PO.

Next asks:
1) Procurement PO or intent to purchase (email/procurement contact)
2) Confirmation on desired region and tranche activation window
3) Any compliance exceptions we should pre-clear before handing to legal

Thanks — Karthik

Aisha / team —

Thanks for the clear plan and the call Friday. We ran this past procurement and they are onboard with the two-tranche approach. Summary of our commitments: 

- NovaMed will issue a PO for tranche 1 (pilot) covering 25% of target capacity; PO attached (PO_NovaMed_7312.pdf). Procurement contact: procurement@novamed.com
- Target onboarding week for tranche 1: week of Nov 22, 2026. We need onboarded canary traffic within that week.
- Tranche 2 activation: target window Dec 20 — Jan 10 (we'll provide 30-day notice to Redwood).
- Compliance: procurement needs the SOC2 summary and the small runbook referenced (Marissa, please send the secure link).

A few small asks:
- Please confirm the acceptance SLOs in writing (latency & sample pass rate) so procurement can include them in the PO appendix.
- Can Redwood provide a short rollback plan in case we hit an unforeseen regression during tranche 2 activation?

Once we have the SLOs and SOC2 link, procurement will sign and wire initial deposit per the PO terms. Looking forward to moving quickly.

Carlos Vega
VP Product — NovaMed
